transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Sara Malik (CTO, Zenith), Derek Huang (Head of MLOps), Priya Shah (Security & Compliance), Evan Clarke (Infra)

Summary (auto): POC scoping call to align on networking topology (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region/residency constraints, benchmark targets and timeline. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, I'm Lina from Redwood, AE on this account. We have Marco, our SE, and we'll run through the POC goals and networking options. Sara, Derek, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Sara Malik: Yep thanks, Lina. Quick note, we have Priya and Evan from infra/security on the line. We're primarily worried about PHI and egress, and we want the service in a private deployment pattern if possible.
[00:32] Marco Reyes: Great. To start, can you confirm whether Zenith requires the inference traffic to stay in your VPC or whether a managed PrivateLink endpoint is acceptable? There's a cost/complexity tradeoff between peering and PrivateLink.
[00:45] Derek Huang: Ideally we'd like no traffic to traverse the public internet, encryption in transit, and egress must be restricted to US regions only. PrivateLink would be preferred if it avoids NAT egress.
[01:02] Priya Shah: Also we need audit logs for model invocations, and KMS integration for keys. SOC2 and ISO are required — do you have docs?
[01:12] Lina Park: Absolutely, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs, I'll share links. For private networking we support both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. Peering gives lower latency and direct routing but needs route tables and CIDR planning. PrivateLink hides your subnets but can add per-Gb egress costs and some cold-start latency.
[01:35] Evan Clarke: On CIDRs, we have overlapping address spaces across accounts in some cases, so peering might be tricky. Could PrivateLink avoid that?
[01:45] Marco Reyes: Yes, PrivateLink avoids CIDR overlap because it uses ENIs in your account; you just need to accept the endpoint. For peering you'd need unique non-overlapping CIDRs. There's also Transit Gateway options but that's more complex.
[02:05] Sara Malik: OK helpful. On the POC success criteria — we want to validate both performance and security. Derek, do you want to lay out the performance targets?
[02:14] Derek Huang: Sure. For our chat assistant, we expect p95 under 120ms for generation at about 50 concurrent requests (roughly 50 rps sustained). We'll also test burst up to 200 rps for short periods. Memory footprint per request varies; typical prompt+history is around 1.5–2k tokens. We'll also want an embeddings job batch test for nightly processing — about 20k docs, 100k embeddings in a run.
[02:40] Marco Reyes: Good detail. For POC we usually run a benchmark matrix: single-request latency, sustained throughput with batching and KV cache on/off, and a large embedding batch run. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail latency, and token/sec.
[02:58] Priya Shah: Important: we can't have any PHI leave the US region. Does Redwood support region pinning for Private deployments?
[03:07] Lina Park: Yes, for Redwood Private we can pin to a region. For Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) we can provision in US-East or US-West regions and ensure the inference runtime runs in that region only. We'll log all request metadata and can integrate with your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 logs.
[03:27] Sara Malik: How about KMS? We need customer-managed keys (CMKs).
[03:32] Marco Reyes: We support customer KMS integration; for Private deployments you can bring your own CMKs, and we integrate with AWS KMS or external HSM via standard APIs.
[03:41] Evan Clarke: Network egress: if we use PrivateLink, will there still be NATting for egress to other AWS services? We want to make sure embeddings output doesn't call external APIs, etc.
[03:55] Lina Park: Good question. PrivateLink keeps the inference API traffic within AWS backbone, but if the model or runtime needs to pull external artifacts during cold start that's configurable. We can lock images and model weights to an internal artifact repo. We'll document and lock egress rules.
[04:15] Derek Huang: For the POC timeline — we're targetting a pilot in September with decision in early October. Can we get a 2–3 week POC where you run benchmarks against our workload and we validate networking?
[04:28] Marco Reyes: Yes, a 2–3 week POC is typical. First week is network setup (endpoint acceptance, peering, CIDR mapping), second week benchmark runs, and final days for analysis and adjustments. We'll need infra access and some firewall rules.
[04:42] Sara Malik: What access does Redwood need? We prefer to limit to a service account with least privilege.
[04:48] Lina Park: We can operate with a service role and limited permissions. For PrivateLink we only need to accept the endpoint. For peering, we'll need route table modifications in a controlled manner. We'll provide an exact IAM checklist.
[05:02] Priya Shah: Auditability — can you provide per-request logs with redaction options? We need to ensure PHI can be redacted or not persisted depending on dataset.
[05:12] Marco Reyes: Yes, we can disable persistent logging of request text and only store telemetry. For POC we suggest enabling full logs under controlled environment so you can validate. We'll document retention and redaction controls.
[05:28] Evan Clarke: For sizing, what's the typical GPU types you run and any quantization options? We may need lower cost configs for embeddings.
[05:37] Marco Reyes: We run a mix — A100-like instances for high throughput and multi-GPU serving for larger models; we also support quantized variants and smaller models for embeddings on cheaper GPUs. For Dedicated we can pin GPU types. We'll propose profiles in the benchmark plan.
[05:52] Sara Malik: Can we see a sample benchmark plan?
[05:55] Marco Reyes: Yes, I'll send a test matrix: latency tests (single-shot, with KV cache), sustained throughput tests at 10, 50, 100 rps, burst tests to 200 rps, and a large embeddings batch. We'll also include payload sizes and prompt templates.
[06:10] Derek Huang: Regarding metrics, p95 <120ms is ideal. For embeddings we care about throughput and error rates. Also want to see cost estimates per 1M tokens and per-embedding.
[06:20] Lina Park: We'll provide unit economics based on observed token throughput and a cost model for Dedicated vs Hosted. For private networking, Dedicated private capacity avoids multi-tenant exposure and gives stronger SLA.
[06:34] Priya Shah: One security point: we need SOC attestation and evidence of pen testing.
[06:38] Lina Park: We'll share SOC2 report and our recent pen test summary. Full reports can be provided under NDA if needed.
[06:45] Sara Malik: Sounds good. For the POC, can you support canary small-scale rollout to validate integration with our front-end?
[06:55] Marco Reyes: Yes — we can help set up a canary route with traffic shaping. We'll also instrument traces so you can see per-request latency in your observability stack via our tracing hooks.
[07:08] Evan Clarke: About region pins — if we pin to US-East, is there any traffic that goes to other regions for control plane? We need to ensure nothing goes to EU.
[07:18] Lina Park: For Private deployments we can keep control plane in your VPC, and the control plane endpoints can be in-region. If you want, we can provide a private control plane option in your account. For our hosted services, control plane metadata may go to Redwood's management region, but for POC we'll use Private or Dedicated options to meet your residency needs.
[07:37] Derek Huang: Ok do you have any constraints on model size for Dedicated?
[07:41] Marco Reyes: We can serve up to 70B models on multi-GPU nodes; for >70B there are options but may require model sharding. We'll outline compatible model choices.
[07:52] Sara Malik: For embeddings job we'd prefer batching to minimize cost — what's Redwood's batching behavior?
[07:58] Marco Reyes: We support automatic batching and you can tune batch size and max latency. For embeddings batch jobs we also have dedicated batch workers that prioritize throughput.
[08:12] Priya Shah: Final question from security: are you able to sign a DPA and process data under a BAA?
[08:19] Lina Park: We do have a DPA and are capable of BAA discussions for healthcare customers; we'll route that to legal and share a template.
[08:28] Sara Malik: Good. Any quick notes on costs?
[08:31] Lina Park: We'll produce an estimate once we size the Dedicated instance types and expected throughput; rough guidance during the POC will be given.
[08:40] Derek Huang: For the benchmark payloads, we'll share 100 representative prompt templates and two sizing payloads: chat short (avg 300 tokens), chat long (avg 2k tokens).
[08:55] Marco Reyes: Perfect. We'll design tests for both.
[09:00] --- mid-call technical dive ---
[09:05] Marco Reyes: (technical) On the network side, if you accept PrivateLink endpoints we provide an endpoint service in our account; you create an interface endpoint in yours. For peering, we need to ensure no overlapping CIDR and accept route tables. If you have Transit Gateway we can peer via TGW but that adds complexity.
[09:30] Evan Clarke: We do use Transit Gateway in parts, could be easier if Redwood supports TGW attachment.
[09:37] Marco Reyes: We can support TGW attachments but it needs more setup; we'll add that as an option in the network checklist.
[09:45] Derek Huang: Benchmarks — how do you simulate concurrent open sessions and KV cache effects?
[09:52] Marco Reyes: We use a harness that replays real prompt patterns and manages KV cache per conversation. We'll run with cache on and off to show delta in token cost and latency.
[10:05] Sara Malik: Great. Anything else on compliance?
[10:09] Priya Shah: Also need role-based access controls and SSO integration — we use Okta.
[10:14] Lina Park: We support SAML/Okta SSO and RBAC with audit trails; we'll include a setup guide.
[10:22] --- final 15 minutes: recap and next steps ---
[10:25] Lina Park: Quick recap: 1) Redwood supports PrivateLink and VPC peering; Private can be used to avoid CIDR overlap but has cost tradeoffs. 2) Success criteria: p95 <120ms at 50 rps, burst to 200 rps, embeddings batch of 100k items, SOC2/ISO and KMS/BAA considerations. 3) Timeline: network setup by 2026-08-10, benchmark runs week of 2026-08-17, analysis week of 2026-08-24, decision target early October. 4) Action items and docs to share.
[10:57] Sara Malik: That aligns with our expectations. We'll get Evan to send CIDR ranges and Priya will confirm residency specifics.
[11:05] Evan Clarke: I'll post the subnet CIDRs and expected egress IPs to the shared doc by Friday.
[11:11] Priya Shah: I'll confirm whether we need EU isolation or US-only, and follow up on BAA requirements.
[11:18] Lina Park: Thanks everyone. I'll send the network checklist, SOC2 links, and the benchmark plan. Marco will follow up on the test matrix.
[11:25] Derek Huang: Thanks all, looking forward to the POC.
[11:29] Lina Park: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
notes: Shared artifacts: network-checklist.xlsx (link to be shared), benchmark-plan.md (Redwood to send), SOC2 and ISO links (Redwood)
Customer asked about TGW attachment; Redwood to add as option in checklist
